data.name: Giana
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, the name Giana is derived from the Greek word 'genea', meaning 'race' or 'offspring'. in_hebrew.name: ג'יאנה
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא חנני - אלוהים רחם עליה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ג'יאנה הוא שם שמקורו בשפה האיטלקית ומשמעותו 'אלוהים הוא חנני' או 'אלוהים רחם עליה'. השם נגזר מהשם העברי 'חנה' שפירושו 'חנינה' או 'רחם'. השם ג'יאנה הוא וריאציה של השם ג'ינה שמקורו באיטליה ומשמש שם נערה נוצרי.

in_greek.name: Τζιάνα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Τζιάνα είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος Giana που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός ελεεί' ή 'Θεία εύνοια'. Αυτό το όνομα έχει τις ρίζες του στην εβραϊκή λέξη 'חנה' που σημαίνει 'χάρη' ή 'ελεημοσύνη'. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Τζιάνα συνδέεται με την έννοια της θείας εύνοιας και της προστασίας.

in_latin.name: Giana
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Giana originem habet in Italia et significat 'Deus miseretur' vel 'Dei gratia'. Hoc nomen derivatum est ex hebraeo nomine 'חנה' quod significat 'gratia' vel 'misericordia'. In traditione christiana, nomen Giana refertur ad notionem gratiae divinae et protectionis.

historical_references.reference: Gianna Beretta Molla, an Italian doctor and mother, was born on April 4, 1922. She was beatified in 2001 and canonized in 2004 by the Catholic Church. Gianna is remembered for refusing a therapeutic abortion to save her own life, as she was pregnant with her fourth child and suffering from a heart condition that required immediate surgery. She died on April 28, 1962, but her unborn daughter, who was delivered by caesarean section after her death, survived.

Gianna Maria Sassato, an Italian nun and World War II heroine, was born on April 23, 1914, in the village of Campo Ligure, in the province of Genoa. She joined the Order of the Sisters of Mercy and became a teacher. During the war, she was arrested by the Germans and taken to a concentration camp. There, she organized a secret school for the children of other prisoners and taught them in the evenings, risking her own life. She died on November 24, 1943.
